prize_parts.citation: for the development of targeted protein degradation, in which bifunctional small molecules recruit E3 ubiquitin ligases to destroy chosen proteins

statement.case_for: I keep a single-part prize on targeted protein degradation. After round 1 it is the only candidate in more than one member's preferred configuration (five of eight), it was ranked top three by six members in the opening, and no member disputes the central scientific claim: recruiting an E3 ligase to a target by a designed molecule gives catalytic, event-driven pharmacology, and this has been reproduced independently in many laboratories. Crews and Deshaies conceived and first demonstrated the concept, and Ciulli's structure-guided VHL ligand and ternary-complex work turned it into a design discipline. The citation is deliberately worded around bifunctional degraders so that the names and the words match. As a sole part, the maturity concern is a timing risk on clinical payoff and not a doubt about the science.
statement.case_against: No PROTAC is approved, so the clinical validation that usually underwrites a prize is still prospective, and the committee could reasonably wait. The attribution is the real weakness: a three-name limit leaves out Handa and Ito, whose identification of cereblon explains the only degrader-type drugs already used in patients, as well as Sakamoto, Kim and Gray. Chabes and Brzezinski regard the Handa omission as serious, and a narrow citation does not remove the objection that the prize rewards the engineered version of a mechanism others uncovered. If the committee concludes that PROTACs and glues cannot be separated, my configuration is weaker than the support count suggests.

responses.point: Chabes puts Handa in the trio instead of Ciulli and widens the citation to include thalidomide-analogue molecular glues.
responses.response: This is the most serious alternative to my trio, and I considered it for the chair's question on a single third name. I keep Ciulli for two reasons. First, the cereblon strand is a target-identification discovery about an existing drug, and a fair glue citation would also have to cover Ito, Gray, Sakamoto and Kim, which does not fit three names; a Handa slot would make the prize half-glue and half-PROTAC without crediting either properly. Second, Ciulli's structure-guided VHL work is the part of the field that shows the mechanism can be designed, which is what a chemistry prize should reward. I accept that this leaves a real exclusion, and I would rather state the narrow citation openly than blur it. I also thank you for the point that sequencing is the mature, overdue choice; I keep it as my first alternative.

responses.point: Sparr proposes a two-part prize, Cullis alone for ionizable lipid nanoparticles plus Crews and Deshaies for the PROTAC concept, and asked whether my omission of lipid nanoparticles from my top four was about field or attribution.
responses.response: It is attribution and, to a lesser degree, proximity to the 2023 Medicine prize, not field. I accept your pKa and phase-behaviour argument that this is chemistry. But your own file concedes that Cullis alone understates a team including Hope, Madden, MacLachlan, Anderson and Langer, and the decisive optimisation happened in companies. Pairing it with degradation also cuts the PROTAC part to two names and removes Ciulli, the person who made degraders designable. I would take B049 seriously if the committee could agree on a defensible name set; I have moved it into my alternatives for that reason, but I cannot support a two-part prize built on a one-name part.

responses.point: Aqvist agrees on the trio but wants the citation kept narrow on bifunctional degrader design, and doubts that a two-person sequencing prize is ready.
responses.response: I agree and have tightened the citation to name bifunctional small molecules, so the wording cannot be read as covering glues. On sequencing I accept the correction: Solexa and 454 are separate routes, and a prize limited to Balasubramanian and Klenerman would have to explain the Rothberg exclusion in public. I therefore no longer treat the two-name core as a clean alternative; it is a possible fallback with a known weakness, and not evidence of greater maturity than degradation.

responses.point: Aili says a two-name sequencing prize does not show greater maturity, and wants Ciulli's role discussed if Handa is excluded.
responses.response: I accept your point on sequencing, and I agree that a degrader prize has too many strong names whereas sequencing has a disputed boundary; neither is free of exclusions. On Ciulli, my argument is that the prize should reward the design logic that generalised, namely VHL ligand structure and cooperative ternary complexes, rather than the first observation. If the committee can show that Handa's work generalises as a design principle in the way you doubt, that would change my view, but I have not seen that argument made.

uncertainties: Whether the committee accepts a narrow bifunctional-degrader citation that leaves out the cereblon-glue strand, or whether Handa and Ito must be inside the prize.
Whether the lack of an approved PROTAC is only a timing risk, as I believe, or a reason for the committee to defer.
Whether B049 could be given a defensible name set; if it could, a two-part prize would deserve another look.
Whether sequencing is judged to be chemistry anchored in reversible-terminator nucleotide chemistry, and where the Rothberg boundary falls.
statement.conflict_note: No candidate-specific conflict or recusal need is apparent; my work is in nanophysics, thermoelectrics and molecular motors and I have no tie to any credited name. As chair, I will keep my role neutral and make sure disagreements are recorded and not smoothed over.
